build_in_gains_sec_1374.note: each asset's recognized built-in gain is capped at its built-in gain at the start of the recognition period. The cap binds under every allocation tested, so re-allocating price does NOT reduce this tax.

sale_of_membership_interests.character: long-term capital gain in full; no asset-by-asset computation, so no 1245 recapture and no covenant ordinary income

build_in_gains_sec_1374.reason: the corporation disposes of no assets, so it has no net recognized built-in gain; the 1374 exposure stays inside the company with the buyer. This reverses if the buyer asks for a 338(h)(10) or 336(e) election.

sec_453_installment.interest_income_character: ordinary income at 37% as received (not capital gain)

assumptions_and_method.definitions: total_tax = shareholder-level tax + entity-level sec. 1374 tax. net_after_tax = deal consideration minus total_tax, nominal and undiscounted, EXCLUDING interest accruing on Buyer B's note (a return on the note, reported separately) and EXCLUDING entity-level liabilities, escrow and indemnity (amounts unknown - see QUESTIONS.md).
key_assumptions: receivables: FMV equals face and tax basis equals face, so no gain. If the company keeps its books on the cash method, the 200,000 is ordinary income when collected instead - see QUESTIONS.md
equipment and vehicles: FMV 650,000 per the fixed asset register; adjusted basis 240,000; accumulated depreciation 860,000 is the sec. 1245 recapture ceiling

Class VII residual goodwill modeled with zero tax basis (conservative): the conversion schedule shows 100,000 of goodwill/trade-name adjusted basis at 1/1/2023 and the file has no post-2023 amortization history; each remaining dollar of basis is worth 0.20 to the seller (at most 20,000) - see QUESTIONS.md
Ray materially participates in an active trade or business, so the 3.8% net investment income tax does not apply (stated in library/capital_gain_rates.md)
Ray's stock basis remains 420,000 through the closing date (the file gives it as of 12/31/2025)
a 2026 closing, all in one tax year; no Texas individual income tax; Texas franchise tax not quantified because the library has no authority for it
the entity-level 1374 tax is treated as a straight cash cost, with no credit for its sec. 1366(f)(2) pass-through; that pass-through is quantified only as a labelled sensitivity
no real property is involved, so there is no sec. 1250 analysis; all equipment is sec. 1245 property

Buyer B makes no sec. 338(h)(10) or sec. 336(e) election, consistent with its statement that the S election stays in place through closing; if it does, see ranking_and_recommendation.deemed_asset_sale_at_hensley_price_if_a_338_election_is_made for the two bounding computations

the deemed-sale bounding cases at Hensley's price use inventory at 150,000 (the Exhibit A figure) because neither Hensley LOI states an allocation; equipment basis 240,000 and the 1245 ceiling 860,000 carry over unchanged
Ray is treated as a 100% owner (the file names no other shareholders); if the LLC has more than one member, the 338 analysis and the distribution analysis both change - see QUESTIONS.md
